summary: This House resolution recognizes May as Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander Heritage Month and affirms the contributions of these communities to U.S. history, diversity, and government.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is a purely symbolic recognition of heritage month with no provisions, authorizations, or references to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets.
No references to taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue measures appear in the text.
The bill contains no content related to healthcare systems, coverage, or policy.
Historical incidents involving firearms are mentioned only as examples of past violence; the resolution does not advocate any regulatory changes.
Historical immigration statutes are referenced in a commemorative context, but the resolution proposes no changes to current immigration law or policy.
No connection to reproductive rights or abortion policy exists.
Military service by Asian Americans is acknowledged historically, yet no spending, force structure, or defense policy is addressed.
The resolution has no environmental or climate provisions.
No welfare, entitlement, or social safety-net programs are mentioned.
No education policy, funding, or school-related measures are present.
The text does not engage with drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related issues.
Past hate-crime legislation is cited for context only; the resolution itself creates no new criminal-justice policy.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization provisions appear.
Deficit, debt reduction, or fiscal policy are not addressed.
The resolution does not mention LGBTQ+ rights or protections.
Foreign aid is not referenced.
No voting rights, election procedures, or electoral reforms are discussed.
Technology regulation and privacy issues are absent.
Labor, unions, or workplace policy receive no mention.
Historical discrimination and hate crimes are noted in a commemorative manner, but the resolution enacts no legal changes regarding religious liberty or anti-discrimination policy.
